prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s message is urgent and hopeful: in dark days of Brexit turmoil, a failing democracy and accelerating climate breakdown, the next decade is decisive. If not now, when?

Their programme is a Green New Deal to deliver both climate safety and social justice. Investing over £100 billion a year (with additional UBI funding), it puts the UK on track for net-zero by 2030 while lifting everyone up. Power and wealth are to be shared more fairly; wellbeing will replace GDP as the yardstick of progress; and no community will be left behind.

Key Green New Deal pillars:
- Energy: Replace fossil fuels with renewables; community energy; end subsidies to oil and gas; a rising Carbon Tax to render fossil fuels unviable; no fracking, no new nuclear; expand grids, storage and interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home; deep retrofit 1 million buildings a year; roll out home renewables; replace gas heating; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes annually; higher standards for all new builds; protect renters and end fuel poverty.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail; reopen lines and expand freight by rail; empower councils to run buses and trams; build safe cycleways/footpaths; Frequent Flyer Levy; stop new runways and road-building; end sales of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030 with widespread EV charging.
- Industry: A circular economy with right-to-repair, ten-year warranties and bans on single-use plastics; grants and standards to decarbonise heavy industry; skills and apprenticeships; regional mutual banks; CCS for steel/cement.
- Food, farming & forestry: A ten‑year transition to agroecology; rewilding and urban greening; 700 million trees; cut pesticides; a right to food; support “less but better” meat and a fair farmer-led transition.

To make it happen, Greens will:
- Remain and reform the EU via a People’s Vote, using Europe to drive climate action, social rights, fair taxation and humane refugee policy while safeguarding freedom of movement.
- Grow democracy: proportional representation; votes at 16; an elected second chamber; citizens’ assemblies and a People’s Constitution; curb oligarchic media power; a Digital Bill of Rights; devolve power and resources to councils; a Carbon Chancellor and a Future Generations Act.

Quality of Life Guarantee: reverse austerity; invest in the NHS (+£6bn/yr) and end privatisation; expand mental and reproductive health; boost schools (+£4bn/yr); scrap tuition fees; smaller classes; restore arts and climate/nature education. Deliver secure incomes and homes with a Universal Basic Income (no one worse off), a £12 Living Wage, 35 hours free childcare from 9 months, gig worker rights, rent controls and an end to no‑fault evictions.

Justice and rights: dismantle the hostile environment; humane migration and Windrush justice; tackle discrimination and misogyny; LGBTIQA+ and disability rights; halve the prison population through prevention and restorative justice; end the war on drugs with legal, regulated supply and health-led support.

Nature and animals: a Clean Air Act; ecocide law; right to roam; more protected land and seas; end factory farming, live exports and hunting; recognise animal sentience.

Global justice: aid to 1% of GNI, climate finance and technology transfer; fair trade rules; end arms sales; a peace-first foreign policy.

Paying for it: simplify and toughen taxes on wealth and corporate profits; introduce a Land Value Tax; a rising Carbon Tax; crack down on avoidance; cancel wasteful projects (Trident, HS2, airport expansion, new roads); and borrow for productive green investment while catalysing private capital.

The Greens say they’ve been on the right side of history—and will get the future right. Every Green vote is a vote to make the Green New Deal real.

TEXT_G:
SNP Manifesto 2019 – Summary (within 500 words)

Core argument
Westminster is broken. Brexit chaos and broken promises show Scotland’s interests are ignored. A vote for the SNP is a vote to escape Brexit, protect the NHS, end austerity, and put Scotland’s future in Scotland’s hands through a democratic choice on independence.

Scotland’s right to choose
- The SNP will seek an agreed, legally watertight process (Section 30) for a 2020 independence referendum.
- SNP MPs are willing to support a progressive alliance to lock the Tories out, with Scotland’s right to choose as a red line.
- Independence means governments Scotland votes for, full control of tax and social security, EU membership, no Trident, and NHS protection from trade deals.

Brexit and Europe
- Scotland voted Remain. The SNP will work to stop Brexit: support a UK-wide referendum with Remain on the ballot; revoke Article 50 if no-deal is the only alternative.
- If Brexit proceeds, SNP MPs will defend single market/customs union alignment and EU standards.

NHS and public services
- Demand UK per‑capita health spending to match Scotland’s, increasing Scotland’s funding via Barnett.
- Pass a National Health Service Protection Act to keep the NHS out of trade deals and profit-driven exploitation.
- End austerity; reverse real-terms cuts to Scotland’s budget; help with cost of living (no VAT or NIC rises; fairer energy bills).

Social justice and welfare
- Scrap the two‑child cap and rape clause; halt Universal Credit and punitive sanctions; end the benefits freeze and uprate benefits.
- Protect the Triple Lock; oppose state pension age rises; support WASPI women; restore Pension Credit and free TV licences for over‑75s.
- Build a humane, dignity-and-respect social security system.

Fair work and the economy
- Devolve employment law; extend the real Living Wage; ban exploitative zero-hours; close the gender pay gap with enforceable standards.
- Tackle tax avoidance/evasion; improve SME support; boost productivity and infrastructure via the Scottish National Investment Bank and fair UK investment.
- Reform corporate culture: worker representation on boards, fair executive pensions, climate risk disclosure, prompt payment.

Migration and rights
- Devolve immigration; create a Scottish Visa; end the hostile environment; protect free movement; reduce citizenship costs; end indefinite detention; expand refugee resettlement and family reunion.
- Democratic reform: replace first‑past‑the‑post with STV; abolish the House of Lords; votes at 16; extend the franchise to EU citizens and all with leave to remain; entrench human rights (UNCRC, defend ECHR/HRA).

Climate emergency
- Match Scotland’s world-leading targets (net zero by 2045; 75% cuts by 2030); align with EU environmental rules.
- A Green Energy Deal: unlock renewables (onshore wind, floating offshore, tidal), CCS in Scotland, grid/transmission reform, green transport and heat incentives; oppose fracking.
- Create a Net Zero Fund by ring‑fencing oil and gas revenues for transition; ensure a just transition for workers and regions.

Rural, food and fisheries
- Protect farm funding; deliver convergence cash; defend PGIs; back Scotch whisky and key exports; maintain high standards; compensate sectors hit by tariffs.
- No sell‑out of Scotland’s fishing interests; ensure fair access, equal rules, and Scottish leadership in negotiations.

Security, defence and foreign policy
- Scrap Trident and reinvest in public services and conventional defence; support veterans (housing, rights).
- Keep 0.7% aid; create a Climate Justice Fund; uphold the rules-based international order; support a two-state solution in the Middle East; decolonisation of Chagos.

Record of action
SNP MPs led legal wins against illegal prorogation and no-deal threats, secured post‑study work visas, VAT relief for police/fire, partial farm convergence funds, UC improvements, FOBT stake cuts, and defended Scotland’s interests throughout the Brexit crisis.
